generate_illustrated_image.title: Illustrations and anime
generate_illustrated_image.description: Use this tool for anything drawn, painted, illustrated or anime-style, whatever the subject. For photographs and photorealistic images, use generate_realistic_image instead.

generate_realistic_image.title: Realistic images
generate_realistic_image.description: Use this tool only for photographs and photorealistic images. For anything drawn, painted, illustrated or anime-style (even an illustration of a real-world subject), use generate_illustrated_image instead.
generate_realistic_image.default_guide:
This tool generates realistic/general-purpose images via ComfyUI.
Use natural language to describe the image you want. Be specific about composition, lighting, style, and subject.

Examples:
- A photorealistic portrait of an elderly man with weathered skin, dramatic side lighting
- A cozy coffee shop interior with warm morning light streaming through windows, watercolor style
- A futuristic cityscape at sunset with flying vehicles, cinematic wide shot

Note: The first generation after launching ComfyUI may take 1-2 minutes while the model loads into GPU memory. If the request times out, please retry.

generate_from_reference.title: From a reference image
generate_from_reference.description: Use this tool to draw the one character in a reference image in a new scene, pose, framing or expression, keeping how it looks. To change the reference picture itself, use edit_image; to draw a character without a reference, use generate_illustrated_image.
generate_from_reference.default_guide:
This tool draws the one character in a reference image in a new scene. The reference gives who is drawn and, unless reference_strength is lowered, much of the drawing style; the prompt gives the scene.
Prompts MUST follow this order:

masterpiece, best quality, score_7, safe, 1girl (or 1boy), solo, [framing], [pose and action], [expression], [place, time and light], [the character's appearance tags]

Swap safe for the rating that fits (sensitive, nsfw, explicit).
- Appearance: when you know what the character looks like (you drew the reference, or the user described them), end the prompt with their key appearance tags: hair, eye colour, body features, outfit, and above all the small or unusual details (teeth, a tail's tip, piercings, accessories). They bring back what the reference alone tends to lose. Don't name the character or its series.
- Outfit: by default the character wears the reference's clothes, and other clothes in the prompt are mixed with them. When the user wants other clothes, or fewer, set new_outfit to true: only the head of the reference is used. Describe the new outfit right after 1girl/1boy, leave the old one out of the prompt, and name every body feature the head doesn't show (a tail, wings, an artificial arm, the build). A hat or other headwear in the reference comes along; take it off with edit_image on the result. For clothes swapped on an image you already drew, with the pose kept, use edit_image on it instead.
- Style: decide whether the user wants the reference's drawing style. If they don't ask for another, leave reference_strength out and add no @artist tag or LoRA trigger: at full strength a tag barely changes the style and can shift details such as eye colour. If they want another style (a named artist, their own usual style, a photo turned into a drawing), put its @artist tag or a LoRA trigger listed below right after best quality, and set reference_strength: 0.5 for an @artist tag; for a LoRA trigger leave it out first (LoRAs hold their style at full strength), and use 0.5 to 0.8 if the style is too weak; 0.3 to 0.5 when the reference is a photo, either way. Lower gives more of the style and less of the character; without a style in the prompt, a lower value only gives the model's own look. Below 1, also name the expression.
- Pose: any framing, pose or expression works (back views, crying, action). Ask for a pose that differs from the reference's: the model is trained not to copy it, and a clear pose in the prompt helps.
- One character per image: always solo, and the reference must show one character. Parts the reference doesn't show (legs in a bust-up, the back of an outfit) are guessed; a full-body reference gives more consistent outfits.
Use booru-style tags with spaces, NOT underscores (e.g. 'looking at viewer'). Text later in the prompt has MORE effect.{lora_triggers}
